command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# WarpX is the NOMPI OpenMP build, so OMP_NUM_THREADS is the only parallel knob. It is
# set per-run inside the script; this is just a sane default for anything else.
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
# Threads to sweep, and the box's on-demand rate so the cost column is real rather than
# a guess. Both are passed in rather than hardcoded in the checks.
export SWEEP=1,2,4,8,16 SWEEP_MAX_THREADS=16 INSTANCE_HOURLY_USD=0.63808

echo "== staged bytes must match their pin =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 --ignore-missing \
  || { echo "FAIL: identities.py does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
# --ignore-missing because pins.sha256 also covers upstream's two analysis scripts, which
# are verified at STAGING time and deliberately not shipped to the box.
grep -q identities.py pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: pin file does not cover identities.py"; exit 1; }

echo "== the deck must be in the image =="
D="$(python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.prefix)')/etc/conda/test-files/warpx/1/Examples/Tests/langmuir"
test -s "$D/inputs_base_2d" || { echo "FAIL: upstream deck absent from the image"; exit 1; }
printf "  %s\t%s bytes\n" inputs_base_2d "$(stat -c %s "$D/inputs_base_2d")"
printf "  langmuir files shipped\t%s\n" "$(ls "$D" | wc -l)"

# python3 -u so a killed run still has its output in command.log.
python3 -u identities.py 2>&1 | tee identities.log
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
# WarpX's own logs are separate files spawn never uploads unless declared; collect them.
# Collect ONLY the per-run logs. A first version tarred the run DIRECTORIES, which made a
# file called warpx-logs.tar.gz 65 MB of plotfiles -- useless for the diagnosability this
# is here for, and a 65 MB download for anyone who wanted a log.
( cd /tmp && find . -maxdepth 2 -name 'warpx.log' -print0 \
    | tar -czf /tmp/warpx-logs.tar.gz --null -T - ) 2>/dev/null || true
printf "warpx_logs_tar_bytes\t%s\n" "$(stat -c %s /tmp/warpx-logs.tar.gz 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" >> identities.log
test "$RC" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: an identity failed"; exit 1; }

uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
